key_insight: A multi-agent healthcare framework can reduce unsafe early diagnosis and undetected hallucinations by enforcing structured symptom collection and uncertainty checks before an answer is delivered.
clinical_relevance: The approach aims to improve patient-facing diagnostic support by making LLM-driven systems more complete, more auditable, and less likely to hand off too early.
method: Uses deterministic orchestration instead of LLM-as-a-judge routing
Blocks diagnosis until OLDCARTS symptom fields are fully collected
Computes semantic entropy from 5 independent diagnostic samples to flag divergent outputs
evidence_signal: In simulation on 150 test cases with llama-3.1-70b-instruct patient agents, the full system reached 49.3% diagnostic precision, an 11.3-point gain over baseline, with a significant negative correlation between OLDCARTS completeness and semantic entropy.
watch_item: Results are based on simulated cases, so real-world clinical performance, workflow fit, and safety across diverse patient presentations still need prospective validation.
paper_title: Agentic AI-based Framework for Mitigating Premature Diagnostic Handoff and Silent Hallucination in Healthcare Applications
